output.summary: A large, fast-growing deciduous tree native to eastern North America. It produces edible nuts, usually three inside each spiny burr, which may be eaten raw but are generally preferred roasted. Once dominant in parts of the Appalachian region, it was devastated by chestnut blight during the early to mid-20th century.
output.edibilityNote: Nuts were historically important in North America and may be eaten raw or roasted after removing the brown skin.
